cards.hook: Detection answers 'what?' AND 'where?' for every object in one image.

formula: class + box (x, y, w, h) + confidence
box x, y, w, h + objectness + class scores
example: One prediction: box, objectness 0.94, car .91, person .03 → 'car 0.91'.
cards.memory: You Only Look Once: share the feature map.
cards.trap: The output is a VARIABLE-length set of records, not a fixed single label.
explain: Detection outputs a list of records, one per object: class + bounding box + confidence.
Trying every crop is hopeless (80×80 positions × 3 sizes × 3 shapes = 57,600 crops), and nearby crops repeat work.
YOLO runs the CNN once to get a shared feature map and predicts a box + objectness + class scores at every location in one pass.

cards.title: Intersection over Union
cards.src: Key points about IoU and non-max suppression
cards.visual: <svg viewBox="-5 -5 270 150" class="bsvg"><rect x="0" y="20" width="150" height="100" fill="#6366f1" fill-opacity=".18" stroke="#6366f1" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="50" y="20" width="150" height="100" fill="#f97316" fill-opacity=".18" stroke="#f97316" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="50" y="20" width="100" height="100" fill="#10b981" fill-opacity=".35"/><text x="5" y="15" class="bl">A (0,0)-(6,4)</text><text x="150" y="140" class="bl">B (2,0)-(8,4)</text><text x="75" y="75" class="bl">I = 4×4 = 16</text></svg>
cards.hook: IoU scores how much two boxes overlap, from 0 (none) to 1 (identical).
cards.memory: Shared over Total (don't double-count the shared part).
cards.trap: Union = A + B − I. Forgetting −I gives 16/48 = 0.33.
explain: IoU measures how much two boxes overlap: the shared area divided by the total area they cover together.
Find the overlap rectangle: its width = (smaller right edge) − (larger left edge), same for height (0 if negative). Union = area A + area B − overlap, so the overlap isn't counted twice.

cards.title: Non-max suppression
cards.src: Key points about IoU and non-max suppression
cards.hook: NMS deletes duplicate boxes around the same object.
cards.visual:
BoxScoreIoU with kept B1Decision (thr > 0.4)
B10.95–keep
B20.900.62suppress
B30.700.10keep (next round)
B40.600.40keep (0.40 is not > 0.40)
formula: suppress same-class boxes with IoU > threshold
repeat with the next remaining box
example: Key points: IoU(A, B) = 0.50 with threshold 'strictly above 0.40' and A higher-scoring → suppress B.
cards.memory: Keep the king, remove the clones, repeat.
cards.trap: Equality does NOT trigger suppression when the rule is 'strictly greater'. NMS is per class.
explain: Detectors often fire several boxes on the same object. NMS cleans up: sort boxes by confidence, keep the best, delete every same-class box that overlaps it too much (IoU above the threshold), then repeat with the next best remaining box.
Read the rule carefully: 'strictly greater than 0.5' means a box with IoU exactly 0.5 survives.

cards.title: Semantic segmentation
cards.hook: Beyond boxes: a class for every pixel.
cards.visual:

example: SceneSegmenter(num_classes = 4): logits [N, 4, H, W] → mask [N, H, W].
cards.trap: The decoder RESTORES spatial resolution; the encoder reduces it.
explain: Semantic segmentation labels every pixel. An encoder shrinks the image into features; a decoder grows them back to full size with C scores per pixel; argmax picks each pixel's class.

cheat.title: Detection cheat sheet
rows: sort, keep top, suppress IoU > thr
traps: Subtract the intersection in the union.
Only same-class boxes suppress each other.
Higher threshold → more duplicates kept; lower → risk deleting real neighbours.
